name: no_capacity_resource_unavailable
description: RunPod's most common create-time capacity rejection. Structured JSON error field embedded among plain-text usage/log lines, as runpodctl emits on create failure.

name: no_capacity_no_longer_available
description: A distinct wording variant of the same class surfaced from a live launch (rlrmp2/5ea2a98): a datacenter-specific 'no longer any instances available' rejection that the substring-only classifier missed until structured parsing was added.
stdout: {"error":"There are no longer any instances available with the requested specifications. Please refresh and try again."}

name: permanent_invalid_request
description: A permanent request/configuration error: the provider rejects the create request itself (bad image reference, invalid flag combination, etc.), which cannot succeed on retry or on another datacenter.
stdout: {"statusCode":400,"code":"invalid_request","error":"image reference is not a valid immutable digest"}

name: authentication_unauthorized
description: An authentication/authorization failure: the provider rejects the create call before ever attempting to schedule a pod, so no pod was created and retrying with the same credentials cannot help.

name: ambiguous_malformed_json
description: A truncated/corrupted response body (e.g. from a partially-read stream): not valid JSON, so no structured error field can be recovered and the failure must be treated as ambiguous rather than guessed at.
stdout: {"error":"This machine does not have the reso

name: ambiguous_unrelated_error_text
description: A well-formed but unrelated provider error whose message names no known no-capacity, request, or auth condition. Halting rather than guessing keeps unmodelled provider wording from being silently misclassified.
stderr: internal server error, please contact support

name: ambiguous_empty_response
description: A create call that returns no output at all, for example after a transport failure that lost the response before it could be parsed. The pod's actual creation state is unknown, so this must fail closed.

name: ambiguous_structured_but_unrecognized
description: A structured JSON error field is present, but its message names a condition (an account-level pod limit) outside this classifier's deliberately narrow, incident-derived vocabulary. Recognizing only adjudicated messages, not guessing at new ones, is what keeps the corpus honest.
